session-contract.text: A session fixes network, slot and block hash. The state diagram shows acquisition, repeated reads, expiry and closure. An unavailable checkpoint is refused; the policy for a checkpoint removed by rollback remains undecided.

storage-separation.text: A session selects checkpoint index roots, which resolve references into immutable content. The same view produces witnesses. Payloads survive rollback, while index membership and branch status determine their ledger meaning. The physical mechanism still needs measurement.

decisions.text: Explicit checkpoint selection replaces mixing latest responses. Bounded views make availability commitments finite, and immutable content allows payloads to be shared across views.

open-questions.text: We must decide behavior on fork abandonment, lease bounds, atomic root capture, archive coverage and failure recovery before optimizing storage.
